conventions.convention: Matching objects are boundary-diagram limits over the augmentation base, with M₀=S. Split terms are coproducts of nondegenerate Nq indexed by order-preserving surjections; the identity contributes Np.
A proper hypercover requires proper surjectivity of the augmentation and every matching map; smoothness and projectivity of terms are additional hypotheses.

The blowup lemma assumes an integral finite-type projective complex scheme and a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal; projectivity means a closed immersion into finite-dimensional projective space.
Borel-Moore chains have locally finite support on a locally compact Hausdorff space. Pushforward is defined for proper continuous maps, where proper means compact inverse images of compact sets.
AC is assumed throughout the hyperresolution and mixed Hodge theorems, including inherited resolution, descent, Godement, partition-of-unity and linear-duality choices.
For smooth projective ambient X of pure dimension d, the class map lands in H^(2d−i)(X)(d), of weight −i. Mixed-dimensional ambient spaces use componentwise dimensions.
Restriction-image equality allows any smooth projective compactification, including non-SNC boundary, and a proper possibly singular or reducible source Y.
The nodal example uses the reduced Čech nerve, with degree-p term the diagonal projective line and 2^(p+1)−2 isolated mixed tuples.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. The rational cohomology H^n(Y,Q) of every proper complex algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure with weights at most n. Pullback from smooth quasiprojective U is a mixed Hodge morphism for its logarithmic structure. For proper Y→X with X smooth projective of pure dimension d, the class map H_i^BM(Y,Q)=H_i(Y,Q)→H^(2d−i)(X,Q)(d) is a mixed Hodge morphism with pure image; mixed-dimensional ambient spaces are treated componentwise.

Assume AC. Every proper complex algebraic variety Y admits a split simplicial proper hypercover with every term smooth projective. Two such systems admit a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both over Y. Morphisms of proper varieties lift after refining the source. Degree-n cohomology uses only the skeleton through degree n+1.

Assume AC. For smooth quasiprojective U, any smooth projective compactification j:U→X and a morphism g:Y→U with Y proper, im((jg)*:H^n(X,Q)→H^n(Y,Q))=im(g*:H^n(U,Q)→H^n(Y,Q)) in every degree. Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight n.
A splitting gives isomorphisms from the coproduct of Nq over order-preserving surjections [p]→[q] onto Xp. A proper hypercover has proper surjective augmentation and canonical boundary maps Xp→Mp.

Assume AC. The blowup of an integral finite-type projective complex scheme along a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal is projective over C. Every finite composition of such blowups remains integral and projective.

For a compact Hausdorff space and a commutative coefficient ring, ordinary singular chains and locally finite chains are isomorphic chain complexes, naturally for continuous maps of compact Hausdorff spaces.

concerns.concern: Fact F2 describes descent for a 'bounded-below constructible coefficient complex F', while the cited Statement of thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology assumes F∈D^b_c(X;k), hence bounded constructible coefficients. The actual proof uses only Q_Y, which satisfies the supplier's hypotheses. Align the fact's stated domain with its citation, or explicitly justify the broader extension.

seams_checked.note: The proper-weights proof constructs a metric and a contractible-open neighbourhood basis before invoking singular/constant-sheaf comparison, and carries AC.
Smooth projective hypercover terms satisfy compact Kähler hypotheses componentwise. Pure cohomology, Hodge-de Rham degeneration and cup-product type compatibility are used as supplied.
Triangulation is applied to affine quasiprojective charts, rather than asserting that an arbitrary proper variety is quasiprojective. Open-star charts supply the local contractibility argument.
AC⇒DC is used in its stated direction to meet the partition-of-unity supplier's hypotheses.

The empty-boundary Godement construction and smooth-open logarithmic structure are used with AC. The arbitrary compactification image formula is supported by the supplier's non-SNC domination argument.
The first-quadrant weight-zero cosimplicial hypotheses are checked. Shifted weights, strictness, image substructures, dual filtrations and the Tate sign are preserved.
Analytification and Kähler inputs are applied to smooth projective terms of pure dimension componentwise; empty and zero-dimensional terms are handled explicitly.

The actual constant-coefficient use is faithful, including proper matching maps and the n+1 cutoff. However, the proper-weights theorem's F2 broadens the supplier's D^b_c coefficient domain to bounded-below constructible complexes without an explicit extension argument; recorded as a presentation concern.
The reduced smooth-projective nerve meets the cosimplicial hypotheses. E₂^(1,0)=Q and E₂^(0,1)=0 give a pure weight-zero, type-(0,0) H¹.
Proper matching-map surjectivity is checked for the reduced Čech nerve before descent is applied. Only bounded constant coefficients and finite first-quadrant diagonals are used.

The induction supplier's Construction F uses smooth U′=f⁻¹(U) inside smooth projective X and proper fibre Z for actual restriction-image equality. Its class map retains the twist (n), and untwisting uses H_n^BM(Z)(−n). The image equality also matches [Deligne III, Proposition 8.2.6](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1974__44__5_0.pdf).
